The intended base/trial rebuild is present, but the current source still does not define a consistent free-parameter LM step. Two specific issues remain.

J.T@r should fail on this path. The FD column already uses the full residual, which is the intended Jacobian row length. After a smaller accepted parameter change, the AD coefficient columns therefore use a different pressure map from the rebuilt base/trial costs. Refresh the stored pressure at the exact base parameters before EVERY Jacobian, or construct a base-point coefficient-Jacobian closure with those kernels. Keep its c_l/omega columns replaced by full rebuilt differences. A mixed coefficient-and-parameter directional-difference check of the complete residual at a base distinct from the original stored pressure will test this.

## 2026-10-25T01:57:55.128101+00:00: original-text homogeneous-field attribution now checked

Date 2026-10-25T01:57:55.128101+00:00. Verdict CONFIRMED for the proposition mapping below; no rotating-profile exclusion follows.

Source: Roman Shvydkoy, Homogeneous solutions to the 3D Euler system, arXiv1510.03378v1. The original arXiv HTML was successfully retrieved with Python urllib, including MathML alttext; source.html is retained and text.txt is a local extraction preserving the mathematical alttext. Retrieval URL and SHA256 are in retrieval.json (HTML sha256 1ac6eedbdf7f859c629cf9c5516bbde357b2c48550c16537534f601732c76a2d). No browser scripts were executed.

Method: read the definitions of homogeneous velocity and the sphere fields, then propositions3.1,3.2,5.1,5.2 and the proof of3.2 on1<alpha<2. The paper's tangential v and radial f correspond to v,b in our standalone proof. Its spherical Bernoulli function is H=|v|^2+f^2+2p=2h in our normalization; the factor two does not change zero sets, signs or vanishing moments. Its Omega denotes physical vorticity. Its small scalar omega denotes a spherical vorticity coefficient, not the campaign rotation parameter omega. Its exponent alpha is the same inverse velocity homogeneity exponent. The paper treats ordinary steady homogeneous Euler, not the logarithmically spiraling rotating profile tail.

| Proposition | Content relevant here | Consequence for1<alpha<2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
|3.1|Classifies C1 irrotational homogeneous fields by sphere harmonics and integer homogeneity.|No nonzero irrotational field in the open interval.|
|3.2|For C2 fields and alpha<=2, zero Bernoulli implies irrotationality; a separate alpha0 statement treats constant Bernoulli.|Its direct sphere integration on1<alpha<2 forces the field to vanish. Beltrami fields have constant physical Bernoulli, and homogeneity with nonzero alpha makes that constant zero.|
|5.1|Excludes nonzero C2 axisymmetric homogeneous fields for0<alpha<2.|Includes axisymmetry with swirl and the full interval used here.|
|5.2|Classifies the axisymmetric endpoint alpha2 as radial and alpha0 as irrotational.|An endpoint statement, not required for our strict1<alpha<2 result.|

Thus the cited proposition numbers exist and support the axisymmetric, irrotational and Beltrami subclass statements with the mapping above. The independent proof in theory/homogeneous_steady_bernoulli/PROOF.md remains self-contained and does not need this citation. # Four-state momentum and vorticity readout

Date: 2026-10-25T13:07:48.061413+00:00. Status: completed with two failed array checks. Provisional campaign label C remains appropriate. No acceptance or obstruction claim follows.

## Method and fixed comparison

The independently written NumPy longdouble reader reconstructs the Cartesian momentum terms, curls, weighted residual reductions, pressure-order differences, Gram diagnostics, amplitudes and core-ball diagnostics from frozen arrays. It imports no producer residual or diagnostic routines. It reads every registered state and both quadrature levels. The producer is this lane's independent Cartesian potential and full-space Green-pressure implementation, separate from the numerics lane. This reader does not regenerate its derivatives or pressure source. The reader registration was made after producer completion and acknowledges that earlier scalar summaries were already inspected; it is an arithmetic validation, not a new blind experiment or state selection.

All four states have c_l = 0.45, omega = 0.3 and omega/c_l = 2/3. Their degree-4, eight-radial-channel matched-Gaussian representation and tail-unit gauge are fixed. The standard and half-offset shell sets, pressure orders 18 and 27, and volume quadratures (8,20,40) and (12,28,56) are all included. Translated balls of radii a_eff/2 and a_eff/4, and the origin ball of radius a_eff/16, use separate doubled volume rules. The tail and phase checks and whole-space balances are separately archived. A quadrature comparison on one representation is not representation refinement.

## Result

The reader completed 21418 checks: 21416 PASS and 2 FAIL. All momentum arithmetic and scalar readbacks passed their registered tolerances. The following are fine-volume diagnostic vectors with pressure order 27; sigma_Omega is a reassembled scalar whose underlying direct-versus-stable vorticity consistency fails once for cancelled_best as described below.

| State | rho_u standard | rho_u half-offset | sigma_u max | sigma_Omega R1024 | a_max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| baseline_projected_initial | 0.0848193396 | 0.0928765572 | 2.34653009 | 1.92144579 | 3.4441723 |
| baseline_best | 0.0821194883 | 0.0921643683 | 2.44707411 | 1.93616047 | 3.54268946 |

| cancelled_best | 0.42271416 | 0.419550137 | 92.2145628 | 46.245639 | 448.745194 |

Here rho_u is the residual normalized by the sum of term RMS values, sigma_u is the single-velocity-scale diagnostic, and a_max is the absolute residual diagnostic in the fixed gauge. The full definitions and shell arrays are in the frozen reader and producer registrations. Both shell families must be read; a lower rho_u alone does not establish improvement under SPEC 7.3b.

For the baseline, 400 steps lower rho_u by 3.183% on standard shells and 0.767% on half-offset shells. However, sigma_u increases by 4.285% and a_max by 2.860%. Thus this is not a simultaneous improvement of the registered diagnostics.

For the near-zero-helicity start, 400 steps lower rho_u by 31.237% and 24.793%, and a_max by 2.925%. Sigma_u increases by 2.358%. Both this start and its continuation retain much larger momentum defects than the baseline. The initial whole-space H of about 1.89e-8 is only a numerical scalar cancellation, not an exact zero or profile condition. Its continuation loses that cancellation: the separately checked H is about -5.701 and E_ren about +1.399. A positive E_ren here refutes a blanket negative-energy description of all tested approximations; it is not evidence of an Euler solution.

The additional core-set maxima sigma_u are baseline_projected_initial 0.674403747, baseline_best 0.769561547, cancelled_projected_initial 77.4494025, cancelled_best 73.8999402. Core volume-doubling, pressure consistency and geometry checks pass for all four states. The largest coarse/fine change among the five common diagnostic-vector entries is 6.19904049e-07. These are finite quadrature comparisons, not enclosures of omitted tails or global suprema.

## Retained failure and follow-up

The failed check is cancelled_best, fine volume, standard shell 10, repeated under pressure orders 18 and 27. The two occurrences concern the same vorticity field; pressure does not enter that operator. The shell spans radii 2 to 4. The unweighted array discrepancy between the direct five-term vorticity assembly and the saved stable assembly is 1.026817592000429e-10 against the unchanged registered tolerance 1e-10. Its first attempt stopped before physical points because the hand-entered manufactured expected values were wrong; that attempt is retained. A documented correction changes only those expected values. No tolerance or selected physical point changed. Pointwise high precision will not retroactively pass the full-array check.

- CONFIRMED: these four approximations are far above the original residual targets, and the near-zero-helicity initialization does not provide a competitive momentum residual after 400 steps.

# Physical normalization differential audit

Date 2026-10-25T16:29:16.987449+00:00. Verdict CONFIRMED for the first differential of the intended real normalization on these eight stored inputs. Composition with an Euler objective and use in search remain OPEN.

The independent all-mode representation has 300 raw coefficients and 181 or 184 chart coordinates. The eight configurations have c_l=0.45, omega=0.3 or 1, and omega/c_l=2/3 or 20/9; degree 3, five radial functions and r0=0.3 or 1. All inputs, code and tolerances were frozen before evaluation. Four inputs came from uncommitted trials in the old phase-guard failure runs. This experiment does not accept those trials.

Write v=Tz, q(v)=integral_S2 |F(v)|^2/(4*pi), and c=v/sqrt(4*pi*q(v)). The prior standalone proof gives the differential and its transpose using the exact rational polynomial bilinear form. The producer checks radial annihilation, a raw core direction with zero leading tail, tangency to the mass constraint, and the transpose identity for two chart directions and a cotangent per input. Every nonzero output coordinate receives a strict rational midpoint rounding certificate using an enclosure of pi and an integer square-root enclosure. Fifty- and eighty-digit proposals give identical binary64 outputs.

Result: 11,480 producer checks PASS, zero FAIL, in 185.2 seconds. A separately written SymPy polynomial and Gamma-moment reader passes 35,442 checks with zero failures. The reader recomputes the exact numerators, bilinear and transpose identities, certificates, seed vectors and rounded finite-difference outputs.

For all 16 chart directions, 6 to 8 of the eight registered step sizes pass the 1e-7 unit-floor directional-difference threshold; only two passing steps were required. The smallest observed error per direction ranges from 4.49e-12 to 1.94e-10. The perturbed chart inputs are exact rational z plus or minus h times the stored binary64 direction, and each coefficient output is rounded once. These finite differences diagnose the intended real map. The rounding operation itself is not claimed to be differentiable.

No Euler residual, pressure reconstruction, optimizer, parameter derivative, global gauge equivalence, or S13 production backend was evaluated here. This coefficient normalization is a parameterization of unit tail mass, not a claim that multiplying a physical field is the Euler dilation symmetry. The old phase failures and thresholds are unchanged. Evidence: PROTOCOL.json, CODE_REGISTRATION.json, results.json, READOUT_PROTOCOL.json, readout.json, and the coordinate certificates beside this report.

## 2026-10-26T11:42:30.487182+00:00: Prospective maximum-search pressure coverage requirement

Method: static inspection of the independently written frozen runtime and the literal SPEC domains. No source values, pressure values or Euler fields were computed.

CONFIRMED: PartialPanelGreen.direct_coefficients and PartialPanelGreen.coefficients reject any radius greater than edges[-1]. OriginSafeGreen inherits that domain restriction. Its full-space exterior contribution does not make these methods evaluable at arbitrary exterior target radii. This restriction is consistent with the earlier batteries, whose admitted targets lie within the prepared grid.

CONFIRMED as exact arithmetic from the registered parameters: the D10 terminal battery has integration_anchor 2048 and radial scale 0.3. The dyadic radial_nodes construction places its last finite edge at 0.3 times 2^15, namely 9830.4 in decimal notation. That value is a grid extent, not r_core. The Stage III maximum search includes thin far shells beginning at 2^14 r_core, 2^16 r_core and 2^20 r_core. Without a check of the actual supplied r_core and every other search set, this pressure table cannot be reused there.

Required construction: after all domains and the represented field are frozen, compute a conservative bound M on |y| over their union. For a ball or shell centered at c with outer radius b, sum_i |c_i| + b is such a bound, since |y| <= |c| + |y-c| <= sum_i |c_i| + b. The axis cap is a subset and needs no larger bound. The maximum of these numbers is sufficient. Compute these sums as exact binary rationals and round upward if a floating value is needed. Include the origin as an explicit point.

Before any selected-state evaluation, require the pressure grid's last finite edge to exceed this bound. A fresh radial_nodes build using an integration anchor at least M and the existing two extra dyadic edges provides room in exact arithmetic. Check the actual produced edge as well, because the implementation uses floating logarithms and products. Rebuild the full source table on this registered grid, include the final integral to infinity and the analytic leading source exactly once, and refine source and partial-panel quadratures. This is new source work, not a use of the old table. Neither a clamped target nor a leading-tail Q substitution evaluates the represented field's full-space pressure.

OPEN: the selected-state domain values, expanded source table, source refinement, off-center momentum readings and literal far-shell pressure accuracy. No Euler adapter or expanded source run is released here. Existing in-grid results are unchanged. This requirement is to be included in the adapter registration and the Stage III resource projection.

Source, smoke driver and any already present records are copied byte-identically here; Python AST parses. No watcher, fake process, GPU query or numerical code was executed by this audit.

V2-1 CONFIRMED improvement: source now records pid/start ticks/argv, compares all three before both signals, derives process start from btime and ticks, checks max_retries, catches ProcessLookupError, and continues after queue/running disappears. The old watcher remains rejected. These improvements do not establish the remaining cap requirements.

V2-2 REFUTED, guaranteed timing under W3/W4: after a late TERM, t_kill is actual current monotonic time plus grace, not the registered absolute KILL deadline. Verification then gets a new30seconds, with each nvidia query allowed20seconds and sleeps independent of the cap. The W3 formula reserves only grace+poll+10seconds. A poll-late signal can leave only10seconds for a verification that can take30seconds plus a final20second query. Binding after the TERM deadline is merely logged and still grants the whole grace and verification time. The script can truthfully record within_cap false only after exceeding the cap. Required correction: absolute monotonic TERM/KILL/verification cutoffs derived at bind, subprocess and sleeps bounded by remaining time, and an explicit incomplete-cap status if binding was too late. Recording an overrun is not enforcing the limit.

V2-3 REFUTED, independent absolute UTC guard: t is wall0 plus monotonic elapsed in the loop; both apparent cap and absolute-end comparisons use that same anchored value. No fresh time.time() guard is used in the main loop, grace or verification. Thus an intervening wall-clock change does not implement W2's separate absolute UTC guard. Binding also sleeps min(poll,5) without limiting it to the remaining abs_end interval.

V2-4 REFUTED, GPU-release evidence: nvidia_has reads subprocess.stdout without checking returncode. A failed command that returns a nonzero status with empty stdout is interpreted as no matching PID, hence nvidia_clear true. Only a successful, parseable query can establish absence. An exception is handled as unknown, but a nonzero return code is not an exception here. The30second verification timeout also needs to bound each query, as V2-2. No query was run in this audit. Production use of no_nvidia must be prohibited by the release or an enforced control-only mode.

V2-5 REFUTED, all completion paths prove termination: any identity_ok false is reported as the job having ended, including unreadable or changed argv while the same start-tick process may still be alive. The normal-exit and zombie branches do not verify GPU absence. After signals, the zombie test omits equality with bound start ticks. Identity loss must mean ownership/termination unverified unless the original process is independently established absent; it must not imply completion.

V2-6 OPEN robustness, with concrete uncovered paths: the binding loop, initial proc_stat and btime reads are outside the main try/finally. In the grace loop proc_stat is called twice; process disappearance between those calls can index None and end the watcher through an exception, without the intended verification. bind_timeout is not checked finite and positive, so NaN defeats that limit until abs_end. Queue max_retries accepts False as0 by Python equality; require an integer0 if that is the schema. These are static paths, not executed failure measurements.

V2-7 REFUTED, W9 coverage as presently described: case2 checks a live unrelated argv, not a changed start-tick identity after binding. Case4 externally kills after8seconds and need not hit disappearance between an identity read and a signal. All cases use no_nvidia, so they cannot detect V2-4. The driver prints outputs and exit codes but contains no assertion that the expected result or cap/end comparison passed. A set of eight attempted cases is not eight accepted tests. Completed logs require individual result review. Keep the exact original attempts rather than silently replacing them.

The queue record is read separately and no equality ties its actual path to the worker config argv. Bind the reviewed canonical config path, or state and justify the job-id-only convention; never infer it from a basename collision. Both signals do recheck the frozen full argv after binding, as V2-1 records.

## Required local corrections

**R1-1, REFUTED: repeated global closure ordering, section 5 lines 689 to 693.** The sentence still says that the omega = 1 closure-met state is, at the same parameters, ordered ahead only of the nest8nk8 continuation. This repeats the overly broad statement removed elsewhere. It is ahead under both predicates of that continuation and six degree-6 states: `s10 both10`, `s12 rl3`, `s14b s5`, `s4allm froms7c`, `s7c m2ecore0.25`, and `s9d k100`. Under the five-ratio rule only, it is also ahead of `nest6 p1`. All have c_l = 0.45, omega = 1, omega/c_l = 20/9. Suggested repair: “among the five states compared in note d128 KH, it is ordered ahead only of the nest8nk8 continuation; section 3 gives its wider same-parameter ordering.” The conditional qualifiers remain. This does not require changing the selection.

**R1-2, REFUTED as a permitted state census: the excluded row returns in the new comparisons.** Section 2 correctly says the diagnostic continuation `s11_L6_cl0.45_om+1.0_fixed_cl1ftol` is not a state and its relations are not used. The lead's all-pairs source nevertheless loads that file. Thus 61/671 counts the excluded entry and its 29 same-parameter pairs. The new section 5 statement that 21 saved readings are ahead of `froms7c` also includes that excluded entry. After its removal the figures are 60 readings, 642 same-parameter pairs and **20** readings ahead of `froms7c`, with the same 51 predicate differences and no failure of the implication. Replace the scientific census with those figures. The raw 61/671 inventory may be retained only if explicitly labeled as including the excluded diagnostic entry and not used as a state comparison. No other reported new ahead-set count changes. The earlier lead `predicates.out` uses all 12 shortlist rows and prints 33/66 and 37/66; the gate's 26/55 and 30/55 correctly exclude row 2 and are independently confirmed here.

**R1-3, REFUTED if read as an all-angular maximum: D10's 2.34e-15 figure, section 5.** That is the largest relative change of the 38 shell non-axisymmetric-energy-fraction comparisons. It is not the largest relative change of all 380 angular comparisons. The latter is 2.6831071096351747e-13 (`volume_half_offset_2/1/rho_nl`); the standard-family angular maximum is 2.0143957783642961e-13. Over every recorded error in the two 342-record groups the maximum is 1.4818443510047482e-10, a source-pressure comparison with its own 1e-7 tolerance. All those records pass their retained tolerances. Repair “with largest relative change 2.34e-15” to “with largest relative change of the shell non-axisymmetric fractions 2.34e-15”. No value or verdict needs changing.

The energy calculation is an averaged pressure argument. With E(R)=integral_(B_R)|U|^2 and Phi(R)=integral_(dB_R)(U.n)(|U|^2/2+P), the exact law is

    d(R^(-gamma) E(R))/dR = -(2/c_l) R^(-gamma-1) Phi(R).

The annular bound integral_(R<r<2R)(|U|^3+|PU|)=O(R^(3-3 alpha)) makes the derivative absolutely integrable, with normalized remainder O(R^(-alpha-1)). Multiplication by R^gamma gives the reported O(R^(2-3 alpha)). The proof does not infer a pointwise angular tail from its positive normalized energy.

For the axisymmetric case, the radial equation along a backward trajectory prevents finite-time contact with the axis when the initial cylindrical radius is positive. Smoothness bounds Omega_phi/rho on its entire compact trapped orbit. Its strictly growing backward transport is therefore incompatible with a nonzero value. The resulting curl-free and divergence-free velocity is harmonic; uniform sublinearity, rather than an unproved global derivative bound, makes it constant.

The item 35 conclusions require exact transport identities. Approximate closed trajectories or floating roots do not inherit the infinite-time argument. Conversely, the local contraction theorem is an exclusion of a specified neighborhood and does not require a separate residual estimate once its uniform bounds and proximity hypotheses have been established. These two scopes must not be conflated.

Result: eight claims CONFIRMED at their stated scopes, one numerical application OPEN. No target-wide obstruction, accepted candidate, new numerical result or change from provisional C follows.
